verdict: KLA's revenue jumped 29% to $4.1B as AI chip-building drove demand for its inspection tools, and it kept $1.5B of that as profit.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted, split-adjusted, vs $0.85 a year ago

segments.name: Product
segments.note: Chip-inspection and process-control equipment sold to chipmakers — up 33% from $2,465M a year ago as AI demand lifted leading-edge spending.

segments.name: Service
segments.note: Servicing and supporting the installed base of KLA tools — up 14% from $745M a year ago.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Designing the next generation of inspection and metrology tools.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Selling, general and administrative costs — running the company day to day.

otherDetail: Net non-operating expense of $38M: interest expense was $68M, partly offset by $30M of other income, net.
oneTimers: Non-GAAP net income was $1,603M ($1.22 per share) after adding back $43M of acquisition-related charges, mainly amortization of acquired intangibles.

takeaways.title: AI spending is the growth engine
takeaways.text: Revenue rose to $4,136M from $3,210M a year ago. Semiconductor Process Control — the core business — brought in $3,754M, and management pointed to AI-driven investment in foundry, logic and advanced packaging.

takeaways.title: More than a third became profit
takeaways.text: Net income was $1,549M, a 37% margin, even after $68M of interest expense. Free cash flow was $1,336M in the quarter.

takeaways.title: Cash went back to shareholders
takeaways.text: KLA returned $1,241M in the quarter — $936M of share buybacks plus $305M of dividends — while guiding next-quarter revenue to about $4.7B.

follow100Note: Of every $100 of revenue, $38.14 went to direct costs and $16.83 to research and running the company — leaving $37.45 as profit.
